html:
The Battle of Levounion was fought on 29 April 1091 in Thrace, near the mouth of the Maritsa river. The Byzantine emperor Alexios I Komnenos and his Cuman allies wiped out an invading army of Pechenegs.

The Pechenegs, Turkic nomads from the steppe north of the Black Sea, had raided across the Danube for decades. In 1090 they wintered in Thrace, close to Constantinople, while the Turkish emir Tzachas of Smyrna planned to attack the capital by sea. The empire seemed near collapse.

Alexios won over the Cumans, another steppe people and rivals of the Pechenegs, and together they fell on the Pecheneg camp. The slaughter, of women and children as well as warriors, was so great that Anna Komnene wrote that a whole people was destroyed in a single day. It was the first great victory of the Komnenian restoration. The last Pecheneg raiders were crushed by John II in 1122.
